metadata.description: SatQuery AI — deterministic mock EO scenarios for prototype demonstration

scenarios.question: How much vegetation has been lost in Uttarakhand between 2020 and 2024?
scenarios.expected_answer: Between 2020 and 2024, Uttarakhand lost approximately 143.8 km² of forest and vegetation cover, representing an 18.7% decline. Mean NDVI dropped from 0.72 to 0.61. Primary drivers include urbanisation, agricultural expansion, and logging activity in the Himalayan foothills.

scenarios.question: Analyse Amazon deforestation rates in Para state, Brazil between 2019 and 2023.
scenarios.expected_answer: Para state experienced approximately 8,430 km² of deforestation between 2019 and 2023, a 12.3% loss. 47 active deforestation hotspots were identified. NDVI declined from 0.81 to 0.67 across the monitored area.

scenarios.question: How has Delhi's green cover changed since 2015?
scenarios.expected_answer: Delhi's green cover declined from 298.4 km² in 2015 to 201.7 km² in 2024, a loss of 96.7 km² (32.4%). Mean NDVI dropped from 0.38 to 0.24, reflecting widespread tree felling and green-space conversion to built-up land.

scenarios.question: Is there any evidence of forest recovery in Western Ghats between 2018 and 2024?
scenarios.expected_answer: The Western Ghats show net forest recovery of 145.2 km² between 2018 and 2024. Mean NDVI increased from 0.64 to 0.69. Approximately 187.3 km² of new vegetation was detected, partially offset by 42.1 km² of loss in vulnerable areas.

scenarios.question: Compare NDVI values in Bandipur National Park in summer 2022 vs summer 2024.
scenarios.expected_answer: NDVI in Bandipur National Park declined slightly from 0.74 in summer 2022 to 0.71 in summer 2024, a 4.1% reduction. The park's 874 km² core area remains well-vegetated but shows marginal drying at the southern edges.

scenarios.question: Where are the vegetation loss hotspots in Northeast India in 2023?
scenarios.expected_answer: 23 vegetation loss hotspots detected across Northeast India in 2023. The worst affected district is Dima Hasao with 312.4 km² of combined loss. Key hotspots cluster along the Assam–Meghalaya border and in Mizoram hill tracts.

scenarios.question: How much has Delhi's built-up area increased between 2018 and 2024?
scenarios.expected_answer: Delhi NCR's built-up area expanded from 612.3 km² in 2018 to 789.5 km² in 2024, an increase of 177.2 km² (28.9%). NDBI rose from 0.12 to 0.24, confirming rapid impervious-surface growth along the urban fringe and in Gurugram/Faridabad corridors.

scenarios.question: Analyse Bengaluru's urban expansion between 2010 and 2024.
scenarios.expected_answer: Bengaluru expanded by 300.2 km² (68.1%) between 2010 and 2024. NDBI nearly tripled from 0.09 to 0.31. An estimated 64 lakes have been encroached or degraded during this period of IT-driven urban sprawl.

scenarios.question: Compare urban sprawl between Hyderabad and Pune between 2015 and 2023.
scenarios.expected_answer: Hyderabad expanded more (214.7 km², +41.2%) than Pune (178.3 km², +37.6%) between 2015 and 2023. Both cities show rapid peripheral growth, with Hyderabad expanding primarily north into Medchal district and Pune east towards Hadapsar and Wagholi.

scenarios.question: Has Mumbai's suburban area expanded into Thane between 2016 and 2024?
scenarios.expected_answer: Mumbai's suburban footprint has expanded significantly into Thane, growing by 89.4 km² (22.7%) between 2016 and 2024. This growth has been accompanied by 11.2 km² of mangrove loss along Thane Creek.

scenarios.question: Map urban growth in Jaipur's outskirts between 2019 and 2024.

mock_data.primary_direction: North and East (Amer, Amber, Chomu corridors)

scenarios.expected_answer: Jaipur's urban area expanded by 67.8 km² (19.3%) between 2019 and 2024. Growth is concentrated in the north and east, particularly along the Amer-Amber and Chomu road corridors, driven by residential township development.

scenarios.question: How much of Assam was flooded during the 2024 monsoon?
scenarios.expected_answer: During the 2024 monsoon, approximately 3,847.6 km² (48.9%) of Assam's surveyed area experienced flooding. 28 districts were affected, with peak inundation recorded on 18 July 2024. SAR data from Sentinel-1 was used to penetrate cloud cover.

scenarios.question: Where are the Brahmaputra flood inundation hotspots between 2020 and 2024?
scenarios.expected_answer: 14 recurring flood hotspots were identified along the Brahmaputra valley between 2020 and 2024, covering 892.4 km² of persistently inundated zones. Morigaon district is most severely affected, with annual inundation exceeding 60% of its low-lying land.

scenarios.question: How has the Yamuna river's water extent changed during the Delhi floods of 2023?
scenarios.expected_answer: The Yamuna's inundated area expanded 13-fold during the 2023 Delhi floods, from a normal extent of 3.2 km² to 41.7 km² at peak on 13 July 2023. The floodplain expansion affected 22 low-lying colonies along the riverbank.

scenarios.question: Assess agricultural flooding in Punjab during 2022 monsoon.
scenarios.expected_answer: Approximately 1,243.5 km² (14.8%) of Punjab's cropland was flooded during the 2022 monsoon. Crop health indices suggest 22.3% of affected agricultural land suffered significant damage, primarily in Sangrur and Patiala districts.

scenarios.question: What was the severity and extent of California wildfires in summer 2023?
scenarios.expected_answer: California experienced 2,847.3 km² of wildfire burn in summer 2023, with 34.2% classified as high severity. The Normalized Burn Ratio dropped from 0.61 pre-fire to 0.18 post-fire. 8,431 individual fire detections were recorded.

scenarios.question: How severe was the Maui wildfire in August 2023?
scenarios.expected_answer: The Maui wildfire burned 21.8 km², with 78.4% classified as high severity. The town of Lahaina suffered 3.9 km² of destruction. NBR fell dramatically from 0.42 to -0.23, indicating near-complete combustion of the affected area.

scenarios.question: Is there vegetation recovery in the 2019 Australian bushfire zones by 2022?
scenarios.expected_answer: By 2022, approximately 4,312.8 km² (67.4%) of the 2019 Australian bushfire zones show vegetation recovery. NDVI increased from 0.14 post-fire to 0.51 in 2022, though full canopy recovery may take another 5–10 years.

scenarios.question: Assess crop health in Punjab during the Rabi 2023–24 season.
scenarios.expected_answer: Punjab's Rabi 2023–24 crop health is generally good, with 82.3% of cultivated area classified as healthy (mean peak NDVI 0.71). Approximately 14.7% shows moderate stress, and 3.0% failed — mostly in areas affected by waterlogging in Sangrur district.

scenarios.question: Identify irrigation stress in Maharashtra's Marathwada region in 2023.
scenarios.expected_answer: 39.8% of Marathwada's irrigated cropland (2,134.7 km²) shows irrigation stress in the 2023 pre-monsoon season. Reservoir storage levels stand at just 18.2% of capacity. NDVI values below 0.35 indicate significant crop moisture deficit.

scenarios.question: Compare wheat crop vigour in Haryana between November 2022 and November 2023.
scenarios.expected_answer: Haryana's wheat crop vigour improved by 12.9% from November 2022 to November 2023, with NDVI rising from 0.54 to 0.61. 3,421.2 km² of cropland shows better establishment, likely due to more timely sowing and adequate soil moisture.

scenarios.question: Assess crop productivity in the Nile Delta during the 2023 growing season.
scenarios.expected_answer: The Nile Delta maintains 9,841 km² of productive cropland with mean NDVI of 0.67. Water availability scored 0.72, though 412.8 km² in northern coastal areas shows salinisation effects that reduce productivity. Overall 2023 crop conditions are moderate-to-good.

scenarios.question: Use SAR and optical data to assess Mumbai's coastline changes between 2018 and 2024.
scenarios.expected_answer: Combined SAR and optical analysis of Mumbai's coastline reveals 4.7 km² of land reclamation, 1.2 km² of coastal erosion, and 2.8 km² of mangrove loss between 2018 and 2024. Net land gain is 3.5 km², primarily from the Sewri–Nhava Sheva coastal corridor.

scenarios.question: Analyse Odisha coastline change after Cyclone Yaas (2021).
scenarios.expected_answer: Post-Cyclone Yaas SAR analysis shows 892.3 km² of storm surge inundation along the Odisha coastline. Coastal erosion totalled 28.7 km², while 147.6 km² of shrimp and fish aquaculture was damaged or destroyed.

scenarios.question: Map flooded areas in Bangladesh's coastal belt using SAR in 2023.
scenarios.expected_answer: SAR analysis identifies 6,247.8 km² of coastal Bangladesh as inundated during the 2023 monsoon. An estimated 4.2 million people live within the flood extent. Agricultural losses cover 2,341.5 km² of paddy and vegetable fields.

scenarios.question: Identify the land cover types visible in this satellite image.
scenarios.expected_answer: Land cover classification: Urban 34.2%, Vegetation 28.7%, Bare soil 18.4%, Water 12.1%, Agriculture 6.6%.

scenarios.question: Identify and map water bodies in this satellite image.
scenarios.expected_answer: 7 water bodies detected with total area 24.3 km², including a river channel, 3 reservoirs, and 3 seasonal ponds.

scenarios.question: Find areas around Delhi where vegetation loss and urban expansion happened simultaneously between 2018 and 2024.
scenarios.expected_answer: 83.4 km² of Delhi NCR shows simultaneous vegetation loss and urban expansion between 2018 and 2024 (47.1% of the vegetation-loss zone). Key conversion hotspots: Gurugram north (28.1 km²), Faridabad west (22.3 km²), Noida south-west (18.7 km²), and Bahadurgarh (14.3 km²).

scenarios.question: Track the evolution of Assam floods from pre-monsoon to post-monsoon 2023.
scenarios.expected_answer: Assam's 2023 flood evolution: Minimal pre-monsoon flooding (120.3 km² in April) rapidly escalated to 1,841.7 km² in June, peaking at 3,612.4 km² in July, receding through August (2,987.1 km²) and largely resolving by October (341.2 km²).

scenarios.question: Analyse Bengaluru's simultaneous vegetation loss, urban growth, and lake shrinkage between 2015 and 2024.
scenarios.expected_answer: Bengaluru shows 184.7 km² of vegetation loss, 248.3 km² of urban growth, and 18.4 km² of lake shrinkage (47.3 → 28.9 km²) between 2015 and 2024. A critical zone of 31.2 km² experienced all three changes simultaneously — primarily in the outer ring-road belt north and east of the city.

scenarios.question: Track post-wildfire vegetation recovery in California's Dixie Fire zone between 2021 and 2024.
scenarios.location: Plumas and Butte counties, California, USA
scenarios.expected_answer: Three years after the Dixie Fire (3,897.2 km² burned), 57.5% of the zone shows measurable vegetation recovery. NDVI rose from 0.08 post-fire to 0.44 in 2024; NBR recovered from -0.31 to +0.28, indicating re-establishment of chaparral and early-successional shrubs.

scenarios.question: Map coastal change in Sundarbans between 2015 and 2024.
scenarios.expected_answer: Sundarbans lost 243.4 km² of mangrove cover between 2015 and 2024. Coastal erosion totalled 87.6 km² while accretion added 41.2 km². Sea-level rise of approximately 3.2 mm/year is accelerating cyclone-driven erosion on the delta's seaward fringe.

scenarios.question: What are current wave conditions near Mumbai?
scenarios.expected_answer: Near Mumbai, significant wave height is 2.1 m with a wave period of 8.4 s. Predominant swell arrives from 248° (WSW), with a swell component of 1.7 m and local wind waves of 0.4 m. Conditions are moderate — advisory for small craft.

scenarios.question: What are the wind conditions over the Arabian Sea during June 2024?
scenarios.expected_answer: Southwest monsoon winds dominate the Arabian Sea in June 2024, averaging 38.7 km/h (gust up to 54.2 km/h) from 225° (SW). Three zones of near-gale-force conditions (>50 km/h) are detected south of 15°N, posing hazards to maritime traffic.

scenarios.question: Find areas in the Arabian Sea where wave height is above 3 metres.
scenarios.expected_answer: Approximately 487,320 km² of the Arabian Sea experiences wave heights exceeding 3 m during the June 2024 monsoon. Maximum recorded height is 5.8 m. Four primary high-wave zones are identified in the central and southern Arabian Sea.

scenarios.question: Are there unusual sea-surface temperature anomalies near Chennai?
scenarios.location: Bay of Bengal near Chennai, India
scenarios.expected_answer: SST near Chennai shows a +1.8°C anomaly relative to climatological baseline, with mean surface temperature at 30.4°C. The anomalous warm zone covers 23,400 km². Such warm SST values elevate cyclone intensification risk in the Bay of Bengal during the pre-monsoon period.

scenarios.question: Compare wind and wave conditions around the Andaman Islands between November and January.
scenarios.expected_answer: Conditions around Andaman progressively calm through winter: Wind 24.3 km/h and 1.8 m waves in November → 18.7 km/h and 1.2 m in December → 15.4 km/h and 0.9 m in January. The NE monsoon retreats, bringing fair-weather conditions ideal for marine navigation.

scenarios.question: Identify ocean SST hotspots in the Bay of Bengal during the 2023 cyclone season.
scenarios.expected_answer: Five SST hotspots exceed 30°C in the Bay of Bengal during the 2023 cyclone season, with peak SST of 31.7°C and anomaly of +2.4°C above baseline. Two zones show ideal thermodynamic conditions for tropical cyclone genesis and intensification.

scenarios.question: Find coastal areas near Odisha where strong winds and high waves occurred together.
scenarios.expected_answer: 19,400 km² of the Odisha coastal zone simultaneously experienced high winds (>60 km/h) and high waves (>3 m), focused around the Puri coast where cyclone landfall occurred. Maximum winds reached 78.4 km/h and wave heights peaked at 4.9 m.

scenarios.question: Find agricultural areas in Punjab showing both crop stress and flooding.
scenarios.expected_answer: 847.3 km² of Punjab's cropland shows both flooding and crop stress simultaneously (10.1% of cultivated area). Sangrur district is worst affected, where waterlogged paddy fields compounded by late monsoon heat stress account for 312.4 km² of combined distress.

scenarios.question: Give me an environmental risk summary for Mumbai including urban growth, vegetation loss, flooding and ocean conditions.
scenarios.expected_answer: Mumbai Environmental Risk Summary (2018–2024): Urban growth: +89.4 km². Vegetation loss: -34.2 km². Mangrove loss: -11.2 km². Flood-risk zone: 47.8 km². Ocean SST anomaly: +1.2°C. Current wave height: 2.1 m. Composite risk score: 0.74/1.0 (HIGH). Mumbai faces compounding risks from urban densification, ecosystem degradation, and intensifying coastal weather.

scenarios.question: What data would you use to investigate a cyclone affecting the Bay of Bengal?
scenarios.expected_answer: Investigating Bay of Bengal cyclone Midhili: Sentinel-1 SAR reveals storm-surge inundation and sea-state anomalies. Ocean data shows genesis over 30.8°C SST. Peak winds 85 km/h, storm surge 1.8 m. Landfall on Bangladesh coast. Flood mapping post-landfall using SAR + optical fusion.

scenarios.question: Identify locations along the Odisha coast facing both high erosion risk and population exposure.
scenarios.expected_answer: 8 coastal erosion hotspots along Odisha's coast erode at an average 3.7 m/year. High-risk population-exposure zones total 142.3 km². Critical areas: Chilika Lake mouth, Puri beach, and Gopalpur — all showing accelerating erosion with dense coastal settlement.

scenarios.question: How has Chennai's urban footprint changed between 2014 and 2024?
scenarios.expected_answer: Chennai's urban footprint expanded by 202.7 km² (47.3%) between 2014 and 2024. Growth is concentrated along the OMR/IT corridor, Tambaram, and northern Tiruvottiyur. 28.4 km² of wetland area has been converted, increasing flood vulnerability.

scenarios.question: Map water body expansion in Rajasthan during the 2023 monsoon.
scenarios.expected_answer: Rajasthan's water-body extent expanded 6.9-fold during the 2023 monsoon, from 412.8 km² (pre-monsoon) to 2,847.3 km² (peak). After receding, approximately 187.4 km² represents new or expanded permanent water bodies, primarily in the aravalli foothills.

scenarios.question: Assess crop decline in Western Uttar Pradesh between 2020 and 2023.
scenarios.expected_answer: Western Uttar Pradesh lost 1,930.2 km² of active cropland between 2020 and 2023 (10.3% decline). Of this, 1,124.7 km² was converted to urban/peri-urban use and 805.5 km² became fallow, partly due to groundwater depletion and farmer migration.

scenarios.question: Assess the extent and severity of Greece wildfires in summer 2023.
scenarios.expected_answer: Greek wildfires in summer 2023 burned 1,847.3 km², with 52.3% classified as high severity. Evros and Rhodope regions in NE Greece were worst affected. The massive NBR decline of 0.74 indicates catastrophic vegetation loss across the Alexandroupolis area.

scenarios.question: What is the sea surface temperature trend in the Indian Ocean over the last 5 years?
scenarios.expected_answer: Indian Ocean SST has increased from 28.1°C (2019) to 29.3°C (2024), a warming rate of approximately 0.24°C per decade. 7 SST anomaly events and 84 marine heatwave days were recorded in this period, intensifying coral bleaching risk across the Lakshadweep and Andaman reefs.

scenarios.question: Analyse the relationship between deforestation and increased flooding risk in Meghalaya between 2018 and 2023.
scenarios.expected_answer: In Meghalaya, 247.8 km² of forest loss between 2018 and 2023 correlates strongly with a 34.2% increase in flood frequency in the same zones. 187.4 km² of deforested land also shows increased flood inundation, suggesting deforestation has increased surface runoff by an estimated 28.7%.

scenarios.question: Is deforestation occurring around the Jim Corbett National Park buffer zone?
scenarios.location: Jim Corbett National Park, Uttarakhand, India
scenarios.expected_answer: The Jim Corbett buffer zone has experienced 23.7 km² of vegetation loss (4.9%) between 2019 and 2024. Six deforestation hotspots were identified, with 14.2 km² showing potential encroachment patterns along the eastern boundary near Ramnagar.

scenarios.question: Compare waterlogging extent in Kolkata before and after the 2023 monsoon using SAR and optical data.
scenarios.expected_answer: Kolkata's waterlogged area expanded from 8.4 km² (pre-monsoon) to 47.3 km² at peak monsoon, a 5.6-fold increase. SAR penetrated cloud cover during peak flooding. Drainage recovery to near-baseline conditions took 12 days post-peak.

scenarios.question: Provide a comprehensive land cover change summary for Goa between 2010 and 2024.
scenarios.expected_answer: Goa's land cover has changed substantially from 2010–2024: Forests declined by 84.3 km², urban area grew by 127.8 km², agricultural land shrank by 43.7 km², and water bodies contracted by 7.2 km². Tourism infrastructure and mining activity are the primary drivers.
